questions.question: What does the argument `row.names = FALSE` prevent in `write.csv(df, "out.csv", row.names = FALSE)`?
options: It stops the column names from being written as the first line of the file.
It stops the row labels 1, 2, 3, … from being written as an extra first column.
It stops `write.csv()` from overwriting an existing file that is called `out.csv`.
It stops the rows from being numbered when the file is read back with `read.csv()`.

questions.question: `read.csv("wage_data.csv")` stops with `cannot open the connection` and warns `cannot open file 'wage_data.csv': No such file or directory`, although the file exists on the computer. What is the most likely cause?
options: The file is not comma-separated, so `read.csv()` refuses to open it at all.
The readr package was not loaded with `library(readr)` in this session.
The file is open in a spreadsheet program, which hides it from R.
The working directory is not the file's folder, or the name is misspelt.

questions.question: How does `read_csv()` from the readr package differ from `read.csv()`, which comes with R?
options: It does the same job but returns a tibble instead of a plain data frame.
It writes a data frame to a file, whereas `read.csv()` reads one from a file.
It reads files separated by semicolons, whereas `read.csv()` expects commas.
It is only another name for `read.csv()` and returns exactly the same object.

questions.question: A comma-separated values (CSV) file `prices.csv` has a header line followed by 40 lines, each with 3 values. What does R print for `dim(read.csv("prices.csv"))`?
The file `sales.csv` has the three lines `Year,Region,Sales`, `2021,North,120` and `2022,South,95`. What does R print for `names(read.csv("sales.csv"))`?
options: `[1] "Year"   "Region" "Sales"`
`[1] "Year,Region,Sales"`

questions.question: A data frame `scores` should be saved as `scores.csv` in the working directory, without row numbers. Which call does this?
options: `write.csv("scores.csv", scores, row.names = FALSE)`
`write.csv(scores, scores.csv, row.names = FALSE)`
`write.csv(scores, "scores.csv", row.names = TRUE)`
`write.csv(scores, "scores.csv", row.names = FALSE)`

questions.question: After `d <- read.csv("rent.csv")`, `head(d)` prints the column `Rent` as 520, 610 and 480. Which call shows whether `Rent` was stored as numbers or as text?
options: `head(d)`: text values would be printed in quotation marks.
`str(d)`: it lists every column with its type and first values.
`names(d)`: it lists every column name together with its type.
`dim(d)`: it gives the size and the type of every column.

questions.question: A file `p.csv` was saved with semicolons instead of commas; its three lines are `Item;Price`, `tea;3` and `jam;4`. What does `dim(read.csv("p.csv"))` return?
options: an error, since the file contains no commas

questions.question: After `write.csv(data.frame(City = "Leeds", Pop = 812000), "city.csv", row.names = FALSE)`, the first line of `city.csv` is `"City","Pop"`. What is its second line?
After the header `Name,Age`, the file `ages.csv` has the lines `Ann,23`, `Bo,` (empty age), `Cy,NA` and `Di,41`. What does R print for `is.na(read.csv("ages.csv")[["Age"]])`?
options: `[1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE`
`[1] FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE`
`[1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE`
`[1] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE`

questions.question: In R 4.x, a data frame `df` has a factor column `size` with levels `"S"`, `"M"`, `"L"`. After `write.csv(df, "d.csv", row.names = FALSE)` and `df2 <- read.csv("d.csv")`, what is the column `size` of `df2`?
options: A factor with the levels `"S"`, `"M"`, `"L"`, since the file also stores levels.
A character vector, since the file holds only the labels as text, no levels.
An integer vector of codes 1 to 3, since a factor is written as its codes.
A factor with the levels in alphabetical order, rebuilt by `read.csv()`.

questions.question: After `d <- read.csv("pay.csv")`, `class(d[["Pay"]])` returns `"character"`, although the column holds pay amounts. What is the most likely reason?
options: `read.csv()` reads every column as text, so numbers always need `as.numeric()`.
Some `Pay` cells are empty, and empty cells turn a numeric column into text.
The header `Pay` is text, so the values below it are stored as text too.
At least one cell holds text such as `n/a`; a column has only one type.

questions.question: `getwd()` returns `"/home/ana/course"`. Which file does `read.csv("data/wage.csv")` try to open?
options: `/home/ana/data/wage.csv`
`/data/wage.csv`
`/home/ana/course/data/wage.csv`
`/home/ana/course/wage.csv`

questions.question: The file `wage.csv` is in the folder `/home/ana/course/data`, but `getwd()` returns `"/home/ana"`. Which call makes a following `read.csv("wage.csv")` work?
options: `setwd("/home/ana/course/data")`
`getwd("/home/ana/course/data")`
`setwd("/home/ana/course/data/wage.csv")`
`setwd("data")`

questions.question: The file `team.csv` has the header `Name,Dept` and the lines `Ann,Sales`, `Bo,` (empty department), `Cy,NA` and `Di,HR`. What does R print for `is.na(read.csv("team.csv")[["Dept"]])`?
options: `[1] FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE`
`[1] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE`
`[1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE FALSE`
`[1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE FALSE`

questions.question: The file `club.csv` has the lines `Name,Age,Height,Member`, `Ann,23,1.68,TRUE` and `Bo,37,1.80,FALSE`. After `d <- read.csv("club.csv")`, what does R print for `c(class(d[["Age"]]), class(d[["Height"]]), class(d[["Member"]]))`?
options: `[1] "numeric"   "numeric"   "character"`
`[1] "integer"   "numeric"   "character"`
`[1] "integer" "numeric" "logical"`
`[1] "numeric" "numeric" "logical"`

questions.question: In a survey file, unknown ages were entered as `-99`. After `d <- read.csv("ages.csv")`, a student reports `mean(d[["Age"]], na.rm = TRUE)` as the average age. Why is this result misleading?
options: `-99` is read as a number and averaged in; only empty and `NA` cells become `NA`.
It is not misleading: `read.csv()` reads `-99` as `NA`, and `na.rm = TRUE` drops it.
The minus sign makes `Age` a text column, so the mean is `NA` with a warning.
`Age` becomes an integer column, so the mean is rounded down to a whole number.

questions.question: The file `people.csv` has no header line: its three lines are `Ann,Sales`, `Bo,HR` and `Cy,IT`. After `d <- read.csv("people.csv")`, what are `nrow(d)` and `names(d)`?
options: 3 rows, with the column names `V1` and `V2`.
3 rows, and `names(d)` returns `NULL`.
3 rows, with the names `Ann` and `Sales`.
2 rows, with the names `Ann` and `Sales`.

questions.question: A data frame `df` has the columns `a` and `b`. A script runs `write.csv(df, "w.csv"); df <- read.csv("w.csv")` and later runs the same line again. How many columns does `df` have afterwards?
options: 3 columns: the extra column is added once and then stays.
4 columns: each save adds one more column of row names.
2 columns: `read.csv()` drops the row-name column again.
An error at the second read, as two columns would be called `X`.

questions.question: A session runs `setwd("~/project")`, then `write.csv(d, "clean.csv", row.names = FALSE)`, then `setwd("~/project/plots")`, and finally `read.csv("clean.csv")`. What happens in the last step?
options: R reads `clean.csv` from `~/project`, the folder where it was written in this session.
R searches the folders above `~/project/plots` and finds `clean.csv` in `~/project`.
R stops with an error, because it looks for `clean.csv` only in `~/project/plots`.
R returns an empty data frame, because `clean.csv` does not exist in `~/project/plots`.
